h: Abbey ruins, a famous battle and a market town packed with history
p: At the foot of the hill stand the ruins of Haughmond Abbey, a medieval Augustinian abbey cared for by English Heritage. The remains include fine carved stonework and the shell of the abbot's lodgings, and it is a lovely spot to combine with a walk in the woods. Check English Heritage's opening arrangements before you plan a visit to the ruins.

Haughmond is also close to the site of the Battle of Shrewsbury, fought in 1403 between King Henry IV and Henry 'Hotspur' Percy. The battlefield lies a few miles to the west, near the village of Battlefield, where a church was built to remember the fallen. The story has made its way into Shakespeare's Henry IV, Part 1, so there is a literary link too.
From the higher points of the hill, the views open out across the Shropshire plain, and on a clear day you can pick out the distinctive shape of the Wrekin in the distance.
Allow anything from an hour for a quick loop to a few hours for a longer walk. Paths can be steep and rooty in places, so sturdy footwear is a good idea, especially for little legs.

Back in Shrewsbury, the town is wrapped in a loop of the River Severn and packed with timber-framed buildings and narrow passageways known locally as shuts. Charles Darwin was born here, and his statue stands outside the old library. Shrewsbury Abbey, Shrewsbury Castle and the Quarry park by the river are all within easy walking distance in town, and Attingham Park, a National Trust estate, is just a short drive away.
